claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr contains 20 at.% each of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr.
The processed WTaTiVZr alloy is single-phase and chemically homogeneous.
Multiple refractory elements produce significant lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr.
The multi-principal-element lattice distortion improves dislocation mobility.
The multi-element alloying stabilizes or improves cohesion of grain boundaries at high temperature.
A uniform strained lattice and improved grain-boundary cohesion allow WTaTiVZr to accommodate more plastic deformation.
Lattice distortion produces a more uniform stress distribution.
More uniform stress distribution and facilitated dislocation motion delay localized stress concentrations and crack formation.
Delayed crack initiation and propagation enhance the intrinsic ductility and toughness of WTaTiVZr relative to pure tungsten.
Grain-boundary crack formation is common in pure tungsten under the relevant conditions.
Above 1000 °C, WTaTiVZr will have a higher strain-to-failure than commercially pure tungsten tested under identical conditions.
Above 1000 °C, WTaTiVZr will have a higher fracture toughness K_IC than commercially pure tungsten tested under identical conditions.
Above 1000 °C, WTaTiVZr will have a lower creep rate than commercially pure tungsten under the same load and environmental conditions.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply above 1000 °C under irradiation and thermal cycling representative of plasma-facing-component service.
The mechanism may not apply at ambient or low temperatures because dislocation mobility and grain-boundary behavior differ from their high-temperature behavior.
Processing history and irradiation-induced effects may alter the observed mechanical behavior.
Commercially pure tungsten tested under matched temperature, load, irradiation, and thermal-cycling conditions is the proposed experimental control.
Failure to observe superior plastic strain, fracture toughness, or creep resistance, or failure to observe the proposed microstructural mediators, would reject the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Irradiation is optional in the stated test conditions ('if feasible'), whereas the baseline requires pure tungsten to be tested under the same high-temperature and irradiation conditions.

The proposed alloy-versus-pure-tungsten comparison changes composition, phase constitution, processing history, and likely grain structure simultaneously, so it does not by itself isolate lattice distortion or grain-boundary cohesion as the cause claimed by the hypothesis.
